cases.title: a1: What happened around 14:00?
cases.input: What happened around 14:00?

trials.output: Around 14:00-14:02 deploy #481 went out on checkout-svc (followed shortly by #482 on checkout-svc and #483 on payments-svc) [2]. Right after, the error rate for both services climbed sharply, peaking at 14:14-14:18: checkout-svc's 5xx ratio hit about 8.4% and payments-svc's about 2.7%, versus a much lower baseline earlier in the day [1]. p95 latency for checkout-svc also rose in that window, peaking around 3.5s at 14:18 versus roughly 0.38s before/after [4][3]. The dominant error codes in this window were a mix of 500/502/503/504 responses [5], and failed orders in postgres-orders were already elevated (34 in a half-hour window around the deploy) [6]. Overall this points to deploy #481 (and the closely-following #482/#483) as the trigger for the incident.

cases.title: a3: Explain the panel error-rate-by-service.
cases.input: Explain the panel error-rate-by-service.

trials.output: This panel tracks the share of requests failing with server errors (5xx), broken out per service for whichever services are selected [1]; a rising line means that service's error rate is climbing, and deploy markers overlaid on the chart help spot whether a release coincided with the increase. It is computed from request counters, taking a short 1-minute rate of 5xx responses divided by the rate of all responses per service, so it reflects very recent, near-live behavior rather than a smoothed longer-term average. The 1-minute window is the key choice: it makes the chart responsive to sudden spikes right after a deploy, complementing the single-service peak view shown in "Error rate · peak".

cases.title: a4: How long did it last?
cases.input: How long did it last?

trials.output: The disruption lasted roughly 42 minutes: checkout-svc's 5xx error rate started climbing just after 14:03-14:04 (right after deploy #481 went out around 14:00-14:02), peaked at about 8.4% at 14:14-14:18, stayed elevated above baseline through about 14:30, then dropped off sharply between 14:30 and 14:42 and was back to its normal ~0.33-0.36% baseline by about 14:42[1]. p95 latency on checkout-svc followed the same pattern: it rose with the errors, peaked at about 3.47s at 14:18, and recovered to its normal ~0.38s baseline by about 14:42[2]. So from first deviation (~14:03) to full recovery (~14:42) the incident spanned roughly 40 minutes, with the worst impact concentrated between 14:14 and 14:30.
